answer: A staking bond tied to verifiable work makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock collateral and solve a cipher puzzle whose cost grows with every new identity it spawns, like a vine that thickens as it spreads. Honest agents earn the bond back through useful attestations, while a Sybil farm must fund each fake from scratch, so creating a thousand sock puppets costs a thousand bonds. In a desert of cheap identities, that price is the dune that stops the flood.
